pull.title: KAFKA-20734: Return Node.noNode() for partitions with offline leaders in getPartitionLeaderEndpoint
pull.body:
### Problem
Since the `KRaftMetadataCache` rewrite, `getPartitionLeaderEndpoint` returns `Optional.empty()` when a partition exists but its leader is not a registered broker, most importantly when the partition is offline (leader `-1`).

`TransactionMarkerChannelManager` interprets `Optional.empty()` as "partition deleted": it removes the partition from the transaction and completes the transaction without writing the marker. A commit/abort marker for an offline partition, including one re-enqueued after its leader failed, is therefore silently dropped. The partition is left with a hanging transaction and the commit marker is lost, so `read_committed` consumers stall on it.

### Root cause
A regression from the `KRaftMetadataCache` rewrite in [KAFKA-17573](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-17573). The previous Scala implementation returned `Node.noNode()` when the leader had no registered broker:

```scala
case Some(partition) => Option(image.cluster().broker(partition.leader)) match {
  case None => Some(Node.noNode)
  case Some(broker) => Some(broker.node(listenerName.value()).orElse(Node.noNode()))
}
```

The Java port mapped that case to `Optional.empty()`:

```java
.flatMap(partition -> Optional.ofNullable(image.cluster().broker(partition.leader))
    .map(broker -> broker.node(listenerName.value()).orElse(Node.noNode())));
```

### Fix
If the partition exists, `getPartitionLeaderEndpoint` returns the leader's endpoint for the listener, or `Node.noNode()` if there is none (leader offline, not registered, or without that listener). It returns `Optional.empty()` only if the topic or partition does not exist. The `MetadataCache` Javadoc now states this contract and why it matters: callers may treat `Optional.empty()` as a deleted partition.

### Testing
- `MetadataCacheTest#testGetPartitionLeaderEndpoint`: leader with endpoint, leader without the listener, offline partition, unregistered leader, unknown partition, unknown topic.
- `TransactionMarkerChannelManagerTest#shouldSaveForLaterWhenPartitionIsOffline`: with a real `KRaftMetadataCache`, the marker for an offline partition is kept in the unknown-broker queue, survives a retry, and the transaction is not completed.
- `TransactionsTest#testCommitMarkerIsWrittenAfterPartitionComesBackOnline` (integration): takes a partition hosted outside the transaction coordinator offline, commits, brings the partition back, and verifies a `read_committed` consumer sees the committed record.

All three fail without the fix and pass with it.

### Compatibility / risk
This restores the pre-KAFKA-17573 contract. All callers were reviewed:
- `TransactionMarkerChannelManager`: markers for offline partitions are parked and sent once a leader is available, instead of being dropped. `Node.noNode()` is never used as a destination.
- `NetworkPartitionMetadataClient`: already treats empty and `Node.noNode()` identically (`LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE`).
- `ShareCoordinatorMetadataCacheHelperImpl` / share-group DLQ: already rejects both `null` and `Node.noNode()` leaders.

While a partition stays offline, the send thread re-checks its parked marker in a tight loop, because re-queuing the marker calls `wakeup()`. This is existing unknown-broker queue behavior: it applies today to a leader without the listener, and applied to offline partitions before KAFKA-17573.

JIRA: [KAFKA-20734](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20734)

Reported by Alyssa Huang. The issue was identified, and the fix sketched, by Artem Livshits.

Reviewers: Justine Olshan <jolshan@confluent.io>

Thanks to Alyssa Huang for reporting this and to Artem Livshits for the analysis on the JIRA. This follows the approach sketched there, keeping the existing `Optional` chain style.

I noticed #22680 targets the same JIRA. If reviewers prefer that one, I'm happy to close this PR or contribute the integration test there; the main addition here is an end-to-end test that reproduces the lost commit marker.

A few questions for reviewers:
- Is the integration test in `TransactionsTest` the right level and place, or would you prefer only the unit tests?
- While a partition is offline, the send thread re-checks the parked marker in a tight loop (re-queuing it calls `wakeup()`). This is pre-existing unknown-broker queue behavior, also present before KAFKA-17573. Should I file a follow-up JIRA to bound that retry?
- `MetadataCache.toCluster` seems to have a similar KAFKA-17573 regression: partitions without a live leader are omitted from the `Cluster` instead of being reported with `Node.noNode()` as leader. Worth a separate JIRA?
- Given the Blocker priority, should this be backported to 4.3 and 4.4?

Thanks for taking a look!

More detail on the retry loop mentioned above, in case it helps the review:

While a marker waits in the unknown-broker queue (leader endpoint is `Node.noNode()`), the `TxnMarkerSenderThread` re-checks it in a tight loop until the partition has a leader again:
- `generateRequests()` drains the unknown-broker queue and calls `addTxnMarkersToBrokerQueue()` for each parked marker.
- The leader is still unavailable, so the marker is parked again.
- `addTxnMarkersToBrokerQueue()` always ends with `wakeup()`, so the next `pollOnce(Long.MAX_VALUE)` returns immediately and the thread loops straight back.

With one parked marker I measured about 30,000 `getPartitionLeaderEndpoint` calls per second (0 when nothing is parked). It does not affect correctness: the marker is sent as soon as the partition has a leader, which the integration test in this PR verifies.

This already happens on trunk when a leader has no endpoint for the inter-broker listener, and it was the behavior for offline partitions before KAFKA-17573. So I kept it out of this fix. A possible follow-up would be to call `wakeup()` only when markers reach a real broker queue, and retry parked markers after a backoff (e.g. `retry.backoff.ms`) or on a metadata update. Happy to file a JIRA for that if reviewers agree.
Hey there, this is already being addressed here: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/22680

Thanks @jolshan, and apologies for the overlap with #22680. I only found it after opening this one.

The production change is the same in both PRs, so I don't want to compete on the fix itself. I'd like to point out what this PR adds on top, in case any of it is worth keeping:

### 1. End-to-end reproduction of the lost marker
`TransactionsTest#testCommitMarkerIsWrittenAfterPartitionComesBackOnline` runs the scenario from KAFKA-20734 on a real 3-broker cluster:

- places the partition on a broker other than the transaction coordinator
- shuts that broker down and waits until every live broker reports `NO_LEADER`
- commits while the partition is offline
- restarts the broker and checks that a `read_committed` consumer sees the record

On trunk the marker is dropped, so the consumer never sees the record. The unit tests in #22680 cover the cache and channel-manager logic in isolation. This test also covers controller metadata propagation, the `addTxnMarkersToSend` wiring and the resend after the broker comes back.

### 2. A Javadoc contract that names the caller dependency
The regression happened because KAFKA-17573 changed what `Optional.empty()` meant while a caller still relied on the old meaning. This PR documents that dependency on `MetadataCache#getPartitionLeaderEndpoint`:

> Callers may treat None as a deleted partition, so it must not be returned just because the leader is unavailable.

That should make it harder for a future refactor to bring the bug back.

### 3. Test details
- The broker registers with a real rack, and the test asserts `new Node(0, "foo0", 9092, "rack0")` instead of using `.setRack(null)`.
- Each case in `MetadataCacheTest` is labelled: offline partition, unregistered leader, unknown topic or partition.

- **Retry loop cost:** while a partition is offline, a parked marker triggers `wakeup()` repeatedly. I measured about 30,000 `getPartitionLeaderEndpoint` calls per second for a single parked marker. Correctness is fine, because the marker goes out as soon as there is a leader, but it may be worth bounding.
- **Possible related regression:** `MetadataCache.toCluster` may have a similar KAFKA-17573 regression.
- **Backport:** given the Blocker priority, should this go to 4.3 / 4.4?

### Proposal
I'm happy to close this PR in favour of #22680. Once that's merged, I'd open a small follow-up with the integration test and the Javadoc wording. I can also file JIRAs for the retry loop and `toCluster` if you think they're worth tracking.

commit.message:
KAFKA-20734: Return Node.noNode() for partitions with offline leaders in getPartitionLeaderEndpoint

Since the KRaftMetadataCache rewrite in KAFKA-17573,
getPartitionLeaderEndpoint returns Optional.empty() when the partition
exists but its leader is not a registered broker, e.g. when the
partition is offline (leader -1). Before the rewrite it returned
Node.noNode() in that case, and an empty result only when the topic or
partition does not exist.

TransactionMarkerChannelManager treats an empty result as a deleted
partition: it removes the partition from the transaction and completes
the transaction without writing the marker. A marker for an offline
partition, including one re-enqueued after its leader failed, was
therefore silently dropped, leaving a hanging transaction on that
partition.

Restore the contract: if the partition exists, return the leader's
endpoint for the listener, or Node.noNode() if there is none. Return
Optional.empty() only if the topic or partition does not exist, and
document why callers depend on that distinction. Markers for offline
partitions are then kept in the unknown-broker queue and sent once the
partition has a leader again.

Add tests for getPartitionLeaderEndpoint in MetadataCacheTest, for
retaining the marker in TransactionMarkerChannelManagerTest, and an
integration test in TransactionsTest that commits while a partition is
offline and verifies the commit is visible to a read_committed consumer
once the partition is back. All three fail without this fix.

issue.body:
In `KRaftMetadataCache`, `getPartitionLeaderEndpoint` returns empty when
the previous leader is offline after the refactor.

With this PR, the method now returns `noNode` when the leader partition
exists, aligning with the original Scala implementation.

Changes are covered by unit tests. Please feel free to review.

Reviewers: Kevin Wu <kwu@confluent.io>, Justine Olshan <jolshan@confluent.io>, Vincent Potuček (github:Pankraz76)

timeline.body: Closing in favour of #22680 (merged). The busy-loop follow-up and the end-to-end test from this PR now live in #23993.
